children: , the memory and storage semiconductor manufacturer, gained approximately 1.3% to $936.60 Tuesday morning after unveiling a new 512-gigabyte DDR5 server memory module. The move offered investors some relief after Monday's 5.3% slide, when broader worries around the pace of AI development pressured semiconductor stocks.

Micron's latest module pushes DDR5 capacity to twice the 256GB product it began sampling in May, while delivering speeds of up to 9,200 megatransfers per second. That matters because bigger memory modules can keep more data closer to server processors and reduce unnecessary data movement across increasingly demanding AI workloads. DDR5 is not a substitute for the high-bandwidth memory used beside AI accelerators, but it is another piece of the infrastructure stack Micron is trying to monetize as data-center systems become more memory-intensive.

The valuation picture is much hotter than the product announcement alone. The chart shows Micron at $936.60 versus a GF Value estimate of $635.23, leaving the shares 47.44% above that benchmark. Micron generated $41.46 billion of fiscal third-quarter revenue and $18.3 billion of adjusted free cash flow, so investors are already pricing in enormous AI-driven earnings power. The next test is execution: this 512GB module needs platform qualifications, real server deployments and meaningful volume before it can justify adding another layer of growth to a stock already trading far above its GF Value estimate.

title: Micron Gains 1.4% as 512GB Module Raises the AI Memory Ceiling
